title: A Tryst with Destiny (address to the Constituent Assembly of India)

access.edition_or_version: Constituent Assembly Debates; Selected Works of Jawaharlal Nehru, Second Series, vol. 3, pp. 135-136

mechanics.premise: On the eve of Indian independence, the speaker frames the moment as the redemption of a long-held pledge and a summons to unending collective labour.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Recollection of suffering and struggle moves to sober responsibility and then to a pledged, future-facing commitment.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Future-tense pathway clauses, balanced antithesis (past/future, sleep/awakening), collective first-person plural, accumulation that resolves into a formal pledge; peroration placed at the close.
mechanics.dialogue: Direct address to the Assembly and, through it, to the people of India.
mechanics.point_of_view: Collective 'we' grounded in a national subject, with the speaker as mover of a resolution.
mechanics.tone_relevant_techniques: Names the labour required rather than triumph alone (pathways + agency); refuses ease as the endpoint; pairs vision with concrete social goals (poverty, ignorance, disease); grounds urgency in an actual historical occasion.
mechanics.critical_reception: Regarded as a landmark twentieth-century oration and the canonical statement of Indian civic aspiration.
mechanics.copyright_note: Speech text is under copyright; described analytically only, no passage reproduced.
